text:
Carmen: Quick thread for follow-ups from today's all-hands infra section. Main asks: per-region GPU supply windows, autoscaler handling for 5-60s spikes, and how Dedicated burst "tokens" will work.
Carmen: Also please include any Console/UI signals we can use to route traffic during constrained windows.
Ibrahim: Short summary: H100 allocation is staggered by vendor shipments. Current plan: us-east pilot late June, eu-central ramp mid-July, apac constrained in August. Exact avail depends on final confirmations.
Theo: Will Hosted routes silently move to H100 when available? Any opt-out?
Ibrahim: Hosted will prefer H100 for low-latency endpoints but we won't force-switch pinned models. There will be a Console toggle to opt-out of H100 for a project.
Lena: We had 12s spikes last week and saw full model loads. Any runtime tricks to avoid heavy cold-starts?
Ibrahim: Two fixes: 1) transient warm pool (keep lightweight artifacts alive for ~50s), 2) a burst-token bucket so short bursts consume pre-warmed tokens instead of spinning new pods. Deploy planned next week.
Carmen: Burst-token bucket? please explain in plain terms.
Theo: Burst tokens are like short-lived credits that let the runtime resurrect warmed state quickly. Tokens refill slowly (configurable) and are separate from baseline replicas.
Ibrahim: Example autoscaler knobs we'll publish:
```yaml
autoscaler:
  baseline_replicas: 4
  max_replicas: 120
  warm_pool:
    enabled: true
    size_percent: 10
  burst_token_bucket:
    enabled: true
    capacity: 30  # tokens
    refill_rate_per_min: 6
  transient_ttl: 50s
```
Ibrahim: And a quick `kubectl` to inspect warm pods:
```bash
kubectl -n redwood get pods -l runtime=warm -o=custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,AGE:.status.startTime
```
Carmen: Nice. How will fallbacks be prioritized when H100s run out? Cost or latency first?
Theo: Default is tenant profile -> latency-first -> cost-aware. Fallback order: H100 -> A100-80GB -> A100-40GB (quantized where available) -> mixed CPU pool. We will expose a preference profile in Console per-tenant.
Lena: For Dedicated burst billing: meter peak or consumed minutes? We need predictable invoices.
Ibrahim: Billing preview: baseline = reserved monthly, burst = consumed minutes charged at premium. For large commitments we can offer burst-minute credits at contract signing.
capacity-bot: New note: region-provisioning-board updated (internal link).
Carmen: Console signals request: can we have a capacity webhook or badge? SREs want immediate signal to failover regionally.
Theo: Console team is prototyping a region-capacity badge (green/yellow/red) and an event webhook for capacity-degraded. Target: beta by end of quarter.
Lena: Any plan to surface per-model latency delta when falling back? That will help product routing rules.
Ibrahim: Yes, runtime will log model-variant delta and Console will show sample P95 delta per model when a route uses fallback. ETA: next sprint.
Carmen: Action list please.
Theo: Actions: 1) Publish per-region H100 ETA and update infra board (Ibrahim). 2) Post autoscaler + burst-token docs and example configs (Ibrahim). 3) Draft Dedicated burst billing terms and credit option (Billing ops). 4) Console: region-capacity badge + webhook prototype (Console). 5) Runtime: expose model-variant latency deltas to Console (Runtime). I'll pin this and follow up in #eng-infra.
Carmen: Thanks all :thumbsup: If anyone needs to dig deeper, open a follow-up thread or schedule time with Ibrahim/Theo.
ops-bot: Deploy note: runtime v2.15 rolled to us-east at 2219876600.
capacity-bot: Capacity alert: us-east H100 pool at 78% allocation (internal).
Carmen: Closing this thread for now.
